summary: Reviewed Calder's corporate finance adviser relationships and other referral partners. Agreed to tier the 40 active advisers and give the top tier more partner time and a quarterly deal criteria card. Bank partnerships need more thought and co-investing above the mandate was rejected.

discussion.keyPoints: Of around 40 advisers who have sent deals, about 10 account for most of the qualified flow. Helen said relationships depend on whichever partner knows the adviser.
Mark suggested the leveraged finance teams at regional banks see deals early. Helen was unsure how formal that should be.
Some advisers bring deals above £50m EV. Mark asked about co-investing with a larger fund on those.

recommendations.recommendation: Tier the 40 advisers into A (10), B (15) and C. A-tier advisers get a quarterly lunch with a named Calder partner.
Send A-tier advisers a one-page deal criteria card, updated every quarter with the week 1 target profile.
Set up formal introducer relationships with the leveraged finance teams at three regional banks.
Co-invest alongside a larger fund on deals above £50m EV.
Sponsor the regional M&A awards in Leeds at a cost of £8k.

actions.action: Assign a named partner to each of the 10 A-tier advisers

nextFocus: Look at how Calder supports portfolio companies after completion and uses exited CEOs as references.
nextPreparation: Bring the current post-completion plan template and a list of exited management teams.

tests.question: How did we tier the advisers?
What did we decide about deals above £50m EV?
What are we sending to A-tier advisers?
